title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: OCR scanning of images on Windows devices (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing statements and configuration controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. Two navigation paths stop on the correct settings page rather than at the final selection, and another Microsoft page still describes Purview OCR settings as preview; these are minor corrections.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans OCR detection of sensitive content in images on Windows endpoint devices.
claims.quote: Optical character recognition (OCR) support will detect sensitive content in images and subsequently apply data loss prevention (DLP) policies to prevent exfiltration of that sensitive data on your Windows endpoint devices.

claims.claim: The planned release applies DLP policies to prevent sensitive image content leaving Windows devices.
claims.quote: subsequently apply data loss prevention (DLP) policies to prevent exfiltration of that sensitive data on your Windows endpoint devices.

claims.claim: The release supports JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and image-only PDF files.
claims.quote: This release supports key file types like JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and PDF (image only PDF).

claims.claim: Documented Purview OCR is optional and requires tenant-level administrator enablement.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Learn documents OCR scanning for Windows and macOS devices.
claims.quote: You can scan images in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Windows, and macOS devices.

claims.claim: After enabling OCR, administrators select the locations to scan and groups to include or exclude.
claims.quote:
Select the locations where you want to scan images.
Select the groups that you want included or excluded from OCR scans.

claims.claim: Tenant OCR configuration is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Optical character recognition (OCR).
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
Select Settings.
Select Optical character recognition (OCR) to enter your OCR configuration settings.
Select the locations where you want to scan images.
Select the groups that you want included or excluded from OCR scans.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct configuration page. Extend it to 'Settings > Optical character recognition (OCR) > locations > groups' to include the documented selections, using https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ocr-learn-about.

claims.claim: No Microsoft-documented PowerShell, Graph or other API for tenant Purview OCR settings was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview tenant OCR settings PowerShell Set-PolicyConfig Graph enable optical character recognition. Read ocr-learn-about, Set-PolicyConfig and Graph security-ocrsettings; the Graph resource is case-level and none documents tenant OCR automation.

claims.claim: The bandwidth setting is under Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > Advanced classification scanning and protection.
claims.quote:
go to Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings.
If bandwidth usage isn't a concern, select Do not limit bandwidth. Unlimited to allow unlimited bandwidth use.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct section. For the documented unlimited option, extend it to 'Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > Advanced classification scanning and protection > Do not limit bandwidth. Unlimited', per https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-configure-endpoint-settings.

claims.claim: No Microsoft-documented automation for the Endpoint DLP advanced-classification bandwidth limit was found.

claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.quote: if you configure the DLP condition content contains sensitive information and include a data classifier such as the Credit Card sensitive information type (SIT), Microsoft Purview scans for credit card numbers in both text and images at all of the chosen locations.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each scanned stand-alone image counts as one transaction.
claims.quote: Each image scanned counts as one transaction. This pricing means that stand-alone images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, BMP, or TIFF) each count as a single transaction.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each PDF page is charged separately, so scanning a 10-page PDF counts as 10 scans.
claims.quote: each page in a PDF file is charged separately. For example, if there are 10 pages in a PDF file, an OCR scan of the PDF file counts as 10 separate scans.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 document-processing pricing page lists OCR at USD $0.001 per transaction.
claims.quote:
What's billed? (USD)
Optical character recognition
$0.001/transaction

claims.claim: A scanned image can be used in any number of DLP, insider risk management, auto-labeling and records management policies without extra charge.
claims.quote: Additionally, you can use each scanned image in any number of policies across data loss prevention, insider risk management, auto-labeling, and records management at no extra charge.

claims.claim: Endpoint OCR maintains a device-local cache for 30 days to reduce repeat costs.
claims.quote:
To reduce your OCR costs, the service uses the following caching mechanisms:
For Endpoint, the cache is maintained for 30 days. Caching is local to each endpoint device and only classifiers identified on the image and image hash are stored.
